key_insight: A minimizing-movement framework uses a smooth, convex energy surrogate to construct parametric finite element schemes with one-step energy dissipation for anisotropic curve shortening.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports variationally consistent simulation of anisotropic interface evolution, including area-preserving flows and facet-like geometries.
method: Majorize the anisotropic energy with an iteration-dependent convex surrogate that matches it at the current curve.
Solve a uniquely solvable unconstrained step for any time-step size, assuming nonvanishing elementwise parametric derivatives.
Use convex splitting for strong anisotropy and a scalar constraint for area preservation.
evidence_signal: Numerical tests show approximately expected convergence for smooth isotropic and weakly anisotropic cases, energy dissipation, and area preservation.
watch_item: Strongly anisotropic tests develop mesh-scale oscillations under refinement despite producing sharp facet-like profiles.
paper_title: A minimizing-movement framework for parametric finite element approximation of anisotropic curve shortening flows
